```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A quota limits output rather than collecting tariff revenue. Here we compare
an 80%-of-baseline ceiling with an unconstrained scenario in a differentiated
Logit Bertrand market. Use **trade 0.9.0** and its compatible antitrust dependency.
Prices and quantities below are illustrative common units; the beer labels and
inputs follow the existing package example based on Epstein and Rubinfeld (2004).

## Fit the constrained scenario

`quotaPost = .8` means a ceiling at 80% of the supplied baseline quantity, a
20% reduction in permitted output. `Inf` means no ceiling. Miller owns two
products; ownership must describe the whole portfolio.

```{r quota-scenario}
library(trade)
products <- c("BUD", "OLD STYLE", "MILLER", "MILLER-LITE",
              "OTHER-LITE", "OTHER-REG")
owner <- c("BUD", "OLD STYLE", "MILLER", "MILLER", "OTHER-LITE", "OTHER-REG")
price <- c(.0441, .0328, .0409, .0396, .0387, .0497)
quantities <- c(.066, .172, .253, .187, .099, .223) * 100
margins <- c(.3830, .5515, .5421, .5557, .4453, .3769)
quota <- c(Inf, Inf, Inf, Inf, .8, .8)
tight <- bertrand_quota(prices = price, quantities = quantities,
  margins = margins, owner = owner, quotaPost = quota, labels = products)
q_post <- antitrust::calcQuantities(tight, preMerger = FALSE)
p_post <- antitrust::calcPrices(tight, preMerger = FALSE)
ceiling <- quota * quantities
slack <- ceiling - q_post
tolerance <- 1e-6 * pmax(1, quantities)
results <- data.frame(product = products, baseline_q = quantities,
  ceiling = ceiling, post_q = q_post, slack = slack,
  binding = is.finite(ceiling) & abs(slack) <= tolerance,
  price_change_pct = 100 * (p_post / price - 1))
knitr::kable(results, digits = 3)
```

A finite ceiling binds when the post quantity reaches it within the stated
numerical tolerance. The slack column is in quantity units; `Inf` indicates an
unconstrained product. Price changes are percentages relative to supplied
baseline prices. Inspect the two OTHER products against their ceilings and
compare their price responses with Miller's two unconstrained products.

```{r quota-feasibility, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(all(slack >= -tolerance), any(results$binding),
          all(is.finite(q_post)), all(q_post >= 0))
```

## What is one more unit of ceiling worth?

Quantity slack is not the shadow value. The shadow is the firm's marginal profit
from one additional unit of its own ceiling, holding competitor prices fixed,
in currency per output unit. It is also different from the full equilibrium
response to relaxing all ceilings. This route has no public quota-shadow accessor.

For this example only, each constrained OTHER firm owns **one product**, has
constant marginal cost c, and faces differentiable Logit demand q(p) with
q'(p)<0. Inverting its own demand while competitor prices stay fixed gives

\[
\lambda=\frac{d[(p-c)q]}{dq}=p-c+\frac{q}{q'(p)}.
\]

At a binding upper ceiling this is its local profit value of relaxation. With
Logit slope alpha and market size M, q'(p)=alpha*q*(1-q/M). The calculation below
uses the primitive demand and physical cost slots; constrained margin or
elasticity methods need not report these unrestricted derivatives.

```{r quota-shadow}
primitive_q <- function(p) {
  weights <- exp(tight@slopes$meanval +
                   tight@slopes$alpha * (p - tight@priceOutside))
  outside <- if (is.na(tight@normIndex)) 1 else 0
  tight@mktSize * weights / (outside + sum(weights))
}
q_primitive <- as.numeric(primitive_q(p_post))
constrained <- 5:6
own_derivative <- tight@slopes$alpha * q_primitive *
  (1 - q_primitive / tight@mktSize)
shadow <- p_post[constrained] - tight@mcPost[constrained] +
  q_primitive[constrained] / own_derivative[constrained]
knitr::kable(data.frame(product = products[constrained],
  shadow_currency_per_unit = as.numeric(shadow)), digits = 6)
```

Both displayed shadows are positive even though quantity slack is approximately
zero. They measure local profit per added unit of the respective ceiling, not
an importing-government receipt. This single-product formula is not a recipe
for a multi-product constrained portfolio: its other products' profit effects
and constraint multipliers would also matter.

```{r shadow-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(max(abs(q_primitive - q_post)) < 1e-8, all(shadow > 0))
for (j in constrained) {
  step <- 1e-7
  up <- down <- p_post
  up[j] <- up[j] + step; down[j] <- down[j] - step
  dq <- (primitive_q(up)[j] - primitive_q(down)[j]) / (2 * step)
  dprofit <- ((up[j] - tight@mcPost[j]) * primitive_q(up)[j] -
             (down[j] - tight@mcPost[j]) * primitive_q(down)[j]) / (2 * step)
  stopifnot(abs(dprofit / dq - shadow[match(j, constrained)]) < 1e-8)
}
```

## Compare with a loose ceiling

The next constructor uses exactly the same observations and ownership. Each
constructor calibrates and solves its own scenario; this comparison does not
claim to reuse a fitted game without calibration.

```{r loose-quota}
loose <- bertrand_quota(prices = price, quantities = quantities,
  margins = margins, owner = owner, quotaPost = rep(Inf, 6), labels = products)
comparison <- data.frame(product = products,
  unconstrained_q = antitrust::calcQuantities(loose, preMerger = FALSE),
  constrained_q = q_post,
  unconstrained_price = antitrust::calcPrices(loose, preMerger = FALSE),
  constrained_price = p_post)
knitr::kable(comparison[5:6, ], digits = 4)
```

Read a constrained quantity together with its price. An output ceiling can
raise a seller's price and redirect sales to competitors. Its scarcity rents
are not automatically importing-government tariff revenue; this calculation
specifies a quantity constraint, not a quota-license auction or rent allocation.

## Scope and numerical interpretation

This public quota constructor supports Logit Bertrand. The quota vector is a
multiple of baseline **product quantities**, whereas homogeneous Cournot plant
capacities have a different data layout. `antitrust::calcQuantities()` returns
market-size-scaled quantity shares, so it avoids manually treating shares as
units. Calibration and equilibrium approximation can affect reproduction of
observations; inspect `calcDiagnostics(tight)` before interpreting empirical
results. The small hidden feasibility check above detects an economically
material ceiling violation; it is not proof that an equilibrium is globally
unique.

Do not pass a quota to the fitted tariff wrapper: `TariffGameFit` explicitly
rejects it. For supported lifecycle routes and exact arguments use
`?bertrand_quota` and `?as_trade_fit`. The
[mathematical reference](https://github.com/luciu5/trade/blob/master/doc/tariff_game_math.md)
contains complementarity background. Continue with the
[tariff accounting guide](Reference.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/trade/blob/master/vignettes/Reference.Rmd)) or
[quantity-setting policy models](cournot-tariffs.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/trade/blob/master/vignettes/cournot-tariffs.Rmd)).
